Read `AGENTS.md` at the repo root first. It's the non-Claude-agent operating
protocol (install, read order, trust boundary, common tasks). Claude Code reads
`CLAUDE.md` automatically and can skip ahead.

Every gbrain error, refusal and recommendation follows one machine contract: read
`code`, follow `fix.next` (`run`, `ask_user`, `tell_user_to_run`, `wait`, `report`),
then run `fix.verify`. Exit 3 means stop and ask the user. Full contract:
[`docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md`](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md).

If you fetched this file by URL without cloning yet, the companion files live at:
- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/AGENTS.md` — start here

## Step 1: Install GBrain

<!-- npm-trap + #218 recovery: canonical copy lives in README.md ("Install" warning) — sync edits. -->
> **NEVER install from the npm registry.** GBrain is not distributed on npm; the npm
> package named `gbrain` is an unrelated package. Do NOT run `npm install -g gbrain` or
> `bun add -g gbrain` (note the missing `github:` prefix — that's the trap). The only
> supported sources are `github:garrytan/gbrain` (optionally pinned as
> `github:garrytan/gbrain#latest-stable`, the form the bootstrap flow mandates) and a
> git clone, exactly as shown below.
> If an unrelated npm install is already present, remove it first
> (`npm uninstall -g gbrain` / `bun remove -g gbrain`); `gbrain doctor` also detects this.

> **On Codex or Claude Code?** After the CLI install below, the plugin is the
> fastest way to wire the MCP server + curated skills:
> `codex plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain@codex-plugin` +
> `codex plugin add gbrain@gbrain` (Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add
> garrytan/gbrain` + `/plugin install gbrain@gbrain`). Details:
> docs/mcp/CODEX.md and docs/mcp/CLAUDE_CODE.md.

Default path (Bun 1.4.0 or newer is required — gbrain is a Bun + TypeScript runtime; on an older Bun, run `bun upgrade` first):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain
```

Verify: `gbrain --version` should print a version number. If `gbrain` is not found,
restart the shell or add the PATH export to the shell profile.

> **If `bun install -g` aborts or `gbrain doctor` reports `schema_version: 0`** (Bun
> occasionally blocks the top-level postinstall hook on global installs, so schema
> migrations don't run automatically), the CLI prints a recovery hint pointing at
> [#218](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/218). Run `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --no-autopilot-install`
> to recover. It exits 0 only when the schema is at head. Exit 1 with `migrations_pending` means the schema
> is still behind: another `--yes` repeats the failure, so run `gbrain doctor --json`, tell the user what it
> reports, and fall back to the deterministic install path:
>
> ```bash
> git clone https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain.git ~/gbrain && cd ~/gbrain
> bun install && bun link
> ```

## Step 2: API Keys

Configured cloud providers receive text: embedding inputs, queries and candidate
passages for reranking, and source or retrieved content for LLM extraction and
synthesis. The harness's own model receives the memory it recalls even when
GBrain is keyless. Explain these boundaries before enabling a capability; see
[memory boundaries](docs/guides/memory-boundaries.md#where-text-goes).

Skip API-key setup for the initial keyless memory path. If the user enables semantic retrieval or paid enrichment, configure the selected provider explicitly. GBrain defaults to the Voyage embedding + reranker stack
(`voyage:voyage-4` @ 1024d + `voyage:rerank-2.5` — one key covers both); OpenAI is the
main alternative, chosen at init via `--embedding-model <provider:model>`.
**Need to switch an existing brain's embedding or reranker model?** Follow
the explicit-consent playbook at `skills/migrations/v0.46.3.0.md`. Preview the
work and cost, obtain approval, then migrate; an upgrade never converts existing
vectors or authorizes a paid re-embed.

```bash
export VOYAGE_API_KEY=pa-...          # default embedding + reranker (one key covers both)
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...          # alternative for vector search; also powers automatic fact extraction + chat models
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...   # automatic fact extraction + chat models; also improves search via query expansion
```

Save to shell profile or `.env`, or store in `~/.gbrain/config.json` (file plane).
`gbrain config set <vendor>_api_key` also works for the vendor keys above — those
keys (like `database_url`/`database_path`) are file-plane routed, so the write lands
where the provider pipeline actually reads. For the autopilot daemon, put keys AND process-level env
(`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, proxy vars, custom base URLs) in `~/.gbrain/env` — a 0600
file created by `gbrain autopilot --install` and sourced by the daemon wrapper;
interactive shell rc files never reach daemon shells, and the path honors
`GBRAIN_HOME`. Re-run `gbrain autopilot --install` after editing it so the daemon
reloads. Without any embedding provider, keyword search still works.
Chat-shaped features (automatic fact extraction, enrichment, synthesis, query
expansion) route to whichever supported chat key is present (Anthropic or OpenAI) —
Anthropic when both are set, OpenAI when it is the only one; other chat providers
need an explicit `models.*` pin. With neither key, extraction stays off and memory
comes from agent-authored `## Facts` fences and the `remember` verb.

## Step 3: Create the Brain

**If you are Claude Code**, one command does Step 3 and the MCP registration:

```bash
gbrain setup claude-code --dry-run --json   # the resolved target; writes nothing
gbrain setup claude-code --json             # brain (if none) + MCP + read-context hooks, verified
```

It runs `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` only when no brain exists, and its
`--json` document carries init's first-run decision bundle in `notices`: relay
the search-mode matrix (Step 3.5) and the decisions in one reply. Capture
(`--capture`) and providers (`--providers`) stay off unless the user accepts
them. A coded refusal (`setup_owner_conflict`, `setup_hosted_connection`) means
another owner or a hosted brain holds the target; follow its `fix`.
`--remove` undoes only what setup wrote. Guide:
[docs/guides/setup.md](docs/guides/setup.md). Otherwise:

```bash
gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding     # keyless memory, no server needed
gbrain doctor --json                   # inspect diagnostics and any warnings
```

**The first-run decision bundle.** Init asks every first-run question once, in
one bundle, and does not wait for the answers: it applies defaults and exits 0.
Human output prints it as an `[AGENT]` block; `gbrain init --json` carries it
as a notice of kind `ask` with `decisions[]`:

| Decision | What the user picks | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `search_mode` | `conservative`, `balanced` or `tokenmax`, with the cost matrix (Step 3.5) | the mode init applied, with its reason |
| `writeback` | whether you save salient facts from conversations without being asked | recommended `salient`; off until the user agrees |
| `harness_wiring` | registering gbrain in the harness you run in (Step 5) | the exact registration command for the detected harness |
| `skills_scaffold` | optional bundled skills in the agent workspace | skip |

…") and apply each answer with the command its option names. One round-trip
covers Step 3.5 and the wiring question. Details:
[first run](docs/protocol/AGENT_OPERATOR_v1.md#first-run).

## The onboard surface

`gbrain onboard` is gbrain's activation surface.
Once your brain has any content, run `gbrain onboard --check --json` to
see structured recommendations across 5 brain-health axes (orphans,
stale embeddings, entity link coverage, timeline coverage, takes count).

**On first connect (after `gbrain init`):**
```bash
gbrain onboard --check --json
```
The JSON envelope (`schema_version: 1`) carries `recommendations[]` with
`apply_policy` per item: `auto_apply` (safe to run unattended),
`prompt_required` (needs explicit user consent), or `manual_only`
(pack upgrade, paid takes bootstrap: the user runs it).

**After every `gbrain upgrade`:**
```bash
gbrain onboard --check --json
```
New versions may surface new opportunities. The post-upgrade banner
nudges the user when it runs, but agents should re-probe as a hygiene
step regardless.

**Unattended remediation (cron / autopilot):**
```bash
gbrain onboard --auto --max-usd 5
```
Refuses without `--max-usd N`. Never runs `manual_only` items; it
lists them in `manual_only_skipped`. The autopilot daemon also consults
onboard recommendations on its tick — no explicit agent action needed
for the autonomous path.

**Remote / federated brain installs (MCP):**
The `run_onboard` MCP op (admin scope) lets thin-client agents probe
brain health + drive remediation over OAuth-authenticated MCP. Protected
LLM-bearing handlers (synthesize, patterns, consolidate, takes-bootstrap,
contextual_reindex_per_chunk) require the additional `run_protected_onboard`
scope — admin alone is insufficient. The MCP op returns
`skipped_missing_scope[]` listing what would have run with the right
grants.

**Privacy + consent gates:**
- `gbrain takes extract --from-pages` sends concept/atom/lore/briefing/
  writing/originals page content to your configured chat model (default
  Anthropic Haiku). Refuses to run unless `takes.bootstrap_enabled=true`
  is set in config AND `--yes` is passed. Two-gate opt-in by design.
- Autopilot's auto-apply tier for takes-bootstrap is `manual_only`
  (do not bypass).

**Suppress nudges in CI / scripted environments:**
```bash
export GBRAIN_NO_ONBOARD_NUDGE=1
```
Init and upgrade notices do not skip themselves when there is no terminal:
non-interactive callers get the onboarding nudge, the init decision bundle and
the post-upgrade summary as `[AGENT]` blocks (or the `notices` key under
`--json`), and stdio MCP sessions get the post-upgrade summary once as a notice
block. `GBRAIN_NO_ONBOARD_NUDGE=1` silences the onboarding nudges and the
post-upgrade summary everywhere. Only the remote-brain identity banner stays
TTY-only (`GBRAIN_BANNER=1` forces it, `GBRAIN_NO_BANNER=1` hides it).

{"content": "1|# Connect GBrain to Hermes
2|
3|> This page is the MCP-registration reference for Hermes (the NousResearch
4|> `hermes-agent`). For the full brain install — CLI, engine, skills, dream
5|> cycle — follow [INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md](../../INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md) first;
6|> this page wires the finished brain into Hermes over stdio MCP.
7|
8|Hermes spawns `gbrain serve` as a local stdio subprocess. No server, no tunnel,
9|no token needed. Works with both PGLite and Supabase engines. No machine that
10|stays online? Hosted GBrain at [gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/?ref=hermes-md) is always on.
11|
12|## Register (recommended)
13|
14|```bash
15|printf 'Y\n' | hermes mcp add gbrain --env GBRAIN_HOME=$HOME --connect-timeout 60 --command $(which gbrain) --args serve --surface starter --advertise verbs
16|```
17|
18|The tool list shows the seven memory verbs (`recall`, `remember`, `entity`, …)
19|plus `request_tools`; every other operation stays callable, and `request_tools`
20|lists it and returns its schema. Drop `--advertise verbs` to list every
21|operation.
22|
23|`hermes mcp add` performs a real MCP handshake and tool discovery at add time,
24|then prompts `Enable all N tools? [Y/n/select]:`. Three gotchas, all observed:
25|
26|- **`--args` must be the LAST option.** Everything after it — including a
27|  misplaced `--env` — is swallowed into the server argv. To pass several
28|  environment variables, list them all after ONE `--env` flag
29|  (`--env A=1 B=2`); repeating the flag replaces the earlier values and the
30|  server is saved disabled when its handshake then fails. Put `--env` and
31|  `--connect-timeout` before `--command`, exactly as above.
32|- **Pipe the `Y` in non-interactive contexts.** EOF on the enable-tools prompt
33|  prints `Cancelled.` and saves nothing. The piped `Y` saves the server with
34|  all tools enabled.
35|- **The exit code is 0 even on connection failure or cancel.** Never assert on
36|  `mcp add`'s exit status — verify with `hermes mcp list` and
37|  `hermes mcp test gbrain` (below).
38|
39|## Brain-first instructions
40|
41|Registering the MCP server only makes the tools available. Agents seldom call a
42|brain nobody told them about, so finish the install with:
43|
44|```bash
45|gbrain setup hermes --instructions-only
46|```
47|
48|It writes one short marked block into `$HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md` (default `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`), after your identity
49|text, which stays first and unchanged: before answering any turn,
50|search the brain first, read the best hit, fill gaps with other tools, apply your own
51|access rules, then finish the task. Text outside the markers is never touched, a
52|re-run upgrades the block in place, `--dry-run` previews it,
53|`--no-instructions` opts out (and is remembered) and `--remove` takes it out.
54|`gbrain doctor` warns when the block is missing or out of date. Setup never
55|creates `SOUL.md`: Hermes uses a non-empty one instead of its default identity,
56|so start Hermes once (it seeds the file) or write your identity there first.
57|
58|The same rule also rides every turn. Setup appends a marked `pre_llm_call` shell
59|hook to `$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml` and records its approval in Hermes's
60|`shell-hooks-allowlist.json` for that exact command:
61|
62|```yaml
63|hooks:
64|  pre_llm_call:
65|    - command: "/bin/echo '{\"context\":\"GBrain: before answering this turn, check GBrain first ...\"}'"
66|      timeout: 10
67|```
68|
69|The command is self-contained: it echoes the rule as Hermes's `{"context": ...}`
70|wire shape, starts no gbrain process and needs no path on the Hermes host but
71|`/bin/echo`. Hermes appends that context to each user message, so the rule
72|reaches the model next to the turn instead of only in the system prompt. Text
73|outside the markers is never touched, and a re-run after an upgrade rewrites the
74|command and moves its approval. When config.yaml already has a `hooks:` section,
75|setup prints the entry to add yourself instead; approve it when Hermes asks (or
76|set `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1`). `hermes hooks doctor` checks it: setup runs it
77|when `hermes` is on PATH and exits non-zero with `turn_hook_not_loaded` when the
78|hook is not healthy ([repair](../guides/repair.md#turn-hook-not-loaded)).
79|`--no-instructions` and `--remove` take the hook and its approval out.
80|
81|Hermes lists gbrain's tools only inside `tool_search`'s description, so with an
82|MCP connection the rule also names them (`mcp__gbrain__recall`, `mcp__gbrain__entity`
83|and the rest) and says to find them with `tool_search`.
84|
85|Search results also carry `_meta.brain_hot_memory`, the brain's recent facts.
86|Hermes may pass them to the model; they can include other sessions' facts, so
87|see [the channel's contract](../protocol/MCP_META_CHANNELS.md#brain_hot_memory)
88|before relying on them.
89|
90|## Direct config (equally supported)
91|
92|The add command writes an `mcp_servers` block into `$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml`
93|(default `~/.hermes/config.yaml`). You can write it yourself instead:
94|
95|```yaml
96|mcp_servers:
97|  gbrain:
98|    command: gbrain
99|    args:
100|      - serve
101|      - --surface
102|      - full
103|      - --advertise
104|      - verbs
105|    env:
106|      GBRAIN_HOME: /home/alice-example
107|    connect_timeout: 60.0
108|    enabled: true
109|```
110|
111|To remove gbrain, delete this block (or set `enabled: false` to disable
112|without losing the config).
113|
114|## Always-loaded core memory
115|
116|Hermes does not read MCP server instructions, so core memory
117|([guide](../guides/core-memory.md)) reaches it through a project context file:
118|
119|```bash
120|gbrain compile-context --target hermes --include-core
121|```
122|
123|This writes `.hermes.md` at the git root and adds it to the repository's local
124|exclude file (`.git/info/exclude`), so it is never committed. Rerun it after
125|core changes; `gbrain doctor` names a stale copy.
126|
127|## Verify
128|
129|```bash
130|hermes mcp list           # table row: gbrain ... ✓ enabled
131|hermes mcp test gbrain    # exits 0 and prints the discovered tool list
132|```
133|
134|Then one real round-trip:
135|
136|```bash
137|hermes -z "ask my gbrain brain: what did I import most recently?"
138|```
139|
140|`hermes -z` prints the final answer on stdout (benign notices may appear on
141|stderr). Inside Hermes, gbrain's tools appear namespaced as
142|`mcp__gbrain__<tool>` (e.g. `mcp__gbrain__search`; Hermes releases before July 2026
143|used `mcp_gbrain_<tool>`).
144|
145|## Headless auth + model pin
146|
147|For cron jobs, CI, or any non-TTY run, Hermes needs a provider key and a
148|default model configured without the interactive picker:
149|
150|- Put the key in `$HERMES_HOME/.env`:
151|
152|  ```bash
153|  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
154|  # or OPENROUTER_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY
155|  ```
156|
157|- Pin the model non-interactively (`hermes model` is interactive-only — never
158|  use it in scripts or CI):
159|
160|  ```bash
161|  hermes config set model.default anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
162|  hermes config get model.default   # reads it back
163|  ```
164|
165|## Pair with cron
166|
167|Hermes cron is fully non-interactive, which makes it a natural scheduler for
168|brain maintenance:
169|
170|```bash
171|hermes cron create --name gbrain-sync '0 */4 * * *' 'Run gbrain sync; report only a non-zero exit, with its error code and fix'
172|hermes cron tick    # run due jobs once and exit — deterministic testing
173|hermes cron list
174|```
175|
176|For health, page on `gbrain doctor --alert`, never on `health_score` or a
177|summary of the full doctor report. The score counts advisory warnings (skill
178|routing, coaching) the same as an outage; the alert verdict pages only on the
179|page class ([doctor --alert](../guides/troubleshooting.md#doctor-alert)):
180|
181|```bash
182|hermes cron create --name gbrain-alert '17 * * * *' 'Run `gbrain doctor --alert --json 2>>~/.gbrain/alert-stderr.log` and read its exit code. 0: say nothing. 17: report each alert.items entry with its fix. 18: report only when alert.consecutive_unknown is 2 or more, with each alert.unknown fix. Any other exit: report the exit code and the last lines of ~/.gbrain/alert-stderr.log. Never report health_score.'
183|```
184|
185|The same rule as a plain crontab line (through the
186|[wrapper](../guides/cron-schedule.md#calling-gbrain-unattended)):
187|
188|```bash
189|17 * * * * gbrain-run doctor --alert --json > /tmp/gbrain-alert.json 2>> /tmp/gbrain-alert.err; rc=$?; case $rc in 0) ;; 17) your-notify "gbrain needs action: $(jq -c '[.alert.items[].check]' /tmp/gbrain-alert.json)" ;; 18) [ "$(jq -r '.alert.consecutive_unknown // 0' /tmp/gbrain-alert.json)" -ge 2 ] && your-notify "gbrain health unknown twice in a row" ;; *) your-notify "gbrain doctor --alert failed (exit $rc), see /tmp/gbrain-alert.err" ;; esac
190|```
191|
192|See [docs/guides/cron-schedule.md](../guides/cron-schedule.md) for the full
193|brain maintenance protocol (sync, embed, dream cycle).
194|
195|## Troubleshooting
196|
197|- **`hermes doctor`** — global health check (installation, config, providers).
198|  It's not a per-server assertion; use `hermes mcp test gbrain` for that.
199|- **`agent failed: No inference provider configured`** (exit 1) — Hermes has
200|  no model key. Set one in `$HERMES_HOME/.env` and pin `model.default` as
201|  above.
202|- **Relocating Hermes** — both the installer and the runtime honor
203|  `HERMES_HOME`. All state (`config.yaml`, `.env`, `SOUL.md`, cron, logs)
204|  lives under it; the default is `~/.hermes`. Export it consistently or the
205|  gbrain registration lands in a config file the runtime never reads.
206|
207|---
208|
209|Documented against **Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3)**. Dev-facing observed-behavior
210|notes (exact flag semantics, exit-code caveats, CI pin values) live in
211|[HERMES-CLI-PIN.md](HERMES-CLI-PIN.md).", "total_lines": 211, "file_size": 9235, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

    stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
    env=env, text=True, bufsize=1,
)

_id = 0
def send(method, params=None, notify=False):
    global _id
    msg = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method}
    if params is not None:
        msg["params"] = params
    if not notify:
        _id += 1
        msg["id"] = _id
    p.stdin.write(json.dumps(msg) + "\n")
    p.stdin.flush()
    if notify:
        return None
    while True:
        line = p.stdout.readline()
        if not line:
            raise SystemExit("server closed: " + p.stderr.read()[-2000:])
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        try:

        except json.JSONDecodeError:

        if obj.get("id") == _id:
